content: {"summary":"Both notification‑worker pods experienced slow DNS lookups and occasional EAI_AGAIN errors from 03:00 UTC on 23 July 2026, caused by the cluster’s default ndots:5 configuration that generated many DNS queries, some of which lost UDP replies and triggered 5‑second resolver timeouts.","likely_cause":"Cluster default ndots:5 caused short names to be expanded with multiple search suffixes, leading to many DNS queries; occasional lost UDP replies forced the resolver to wait the 5 s timeout and retry, producing slow lookups and EAI_AGAIN errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The resolver waited the 5 s timeout and retried when a DNS reply was lost, making lookups 5 s late.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#5"],"quote":"resolver waits out its 5 s timeout and asks that query again; the retry usually succeeds"},{"text":"ndots:5 makes a short name generate multiple queries (8 UDP queries per lookup).","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4","INC-0179#0"],"quote":"ndots:5 means a name with fewer than five dots gets each search suffix appended first"},{"text":"Both workers saw slow name resolutions and some lookups returned getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN.","evidence_ids":["RB-021#7","INC-0179#0"],"quote":"getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN for a name that resolves when you try it by hand"},{"text":"The incident lasted from 03:00 to 06:35 UTC, a total of 215 minutes.","evidence_ids":["INC-0179#2"],"quote":"The incident record starts at 03:00 and ends at 06:35, which is 215 minutes"}],"next_checks":["Check the resolver configuration of notification‑worker Deployments for ndots overrides","Monitor DNS UDP packet loss and retry metrics during peak periods","Consider reducing ndots or increasing UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE to mitigate thread contention","Validate if other services with short DNS names exhibit similar latency"]}
